hook: After this article, every closed door looks a little different. The entity is heard far more than it is seen, and the horror lives in the gap between knowing something is on the other side and being unable to make yourself check. It is mostly psychological, but be aware that one test entry involves a prisoner being cut with a knife until she dies.
whyItMatters: The anomaly is defined by a rule of perception: it never lets anyone see more than a tenth of its body, yet everyone who meets it, even people who saw nothing at all, can describe it in full. The file also takes care to say the fear it causes is not deliberate but something closer to an inborn phobia, which makes it stranger rather than safer. The containment plan, rebuilding a whole site so every room has two doors far apart, shows how one behavior can reshape the Foundation's routine.
thingsToNotice: The incidents escalate from intimate to fatal: an agent spends three hours crying silently in her shower with the creature standing upright half a metre away behind the curtain, another senses it curled up in a break-room cabinet that later turns out to be missing coffee creamer, and a doctor dies of dehydration after five days trapped in a storage room because it sat in the only airlock out. The test log is where the Foundation becomes the monster: one D-class who refuses to open the door is executed on the spot, and another is handed a combat knife and ordered to use it on a woman, in redacted ways, until she opens it, and she bleeds out over two hours without ever trying, while what both refusers predicted the creature would do stays expunged. The final inventory shifts the question from what it is to what it is building, as it hoards a cryotube, surgical kits, two D-class cadavers, a generator, amino acids like tryptophan and tyrosine, and that tub of creamer in the storage room it has claimed, and the article never says why.
